rules.applyFieldSpecTargetHost: Matches only the source host. It does not change the downstream target or X-Original-Host.
rules.applyFieldSpecMatchKey: HTTP request path or JMS queue name. Use * as a fallback.
rules.applyFieldSpecMethod: HTTP request method, using one of the listed uppercase standard values.
rules.applyFieldSpecBodyCondition: Request-body condition. Use field=value; !=, *=, and ~= are supported. Separate conditions with semicolons.
rules.applyFieldSpecQueryCondition: HTTP query condition using the same format as bodyCondition.
rules.applyFieldSpecHeaderCondition: HTTP header condition. The ~= value must be a valid regular expression.
rules.applyFieldSpecPriority: Match priority. Higher numbers run first.
rules.applyFieldSpecDescription: Purpose of the rule, up to 255 characters.
rules.applyFieldSpecEnabled: Whether this rule participates in matching.
rules.applyFieldSpecProtected: Whether scheduled cleanup must retain this rule.
rules.applyFieldSpecTags: Labels for grouping and search. Every key and value must be text.
rules.applyFieldSpecResponseId: ID of an existing shared response. Changing responseBody creates and rebinds a new response.
rules.applyFieldSpecResponseBody: Content returned after a match. It may be JSON, an array, or plain text.
rules.applyFieldSpecResponseDescription: Purpose of the response, up to 255 characters.
rules.applyFieldSpecStatus: HTTP status returned by a Mock response.
rules.applyFieldSpecResponseHeaders: Headers returned by an HTTP Mock response. Every key and value must be text.
rules.applyFieldSpecMaxDelayMs: Upper random-delay bound. It must be greater than or equal to delayMs.
rules.applyFieldSpecSseEnabled: Return an SSE event sequence for the HTTP request.
rules.applyFieldSpecSseLoopEnabled: Repeat the SSE sequence. It can be true only when SSE is enabled.
rules.applyFieldSpecResponseContentType: Derived from protocol and sseEnabled; manual editing is unnecessary.
rules.applyFieldSpecAction: Return a Mock response or forward downstream after an HTTP match.
rules.applyFieldSpecForwardTargetMode: ORIGINAL_HOST uses X-Original-Host; DEFAULT_CONNECTION uses the default connection; CONNECTION uses a selected connection.
rules.applyFieldSpecHttpTargetConnectionId: ID of the HTTP connection in Settings when forwardTargetMode is CONNECTION.

help.diagramHttpFlow:
GET /mock/api/users + X-Original-Host
                 │
                 ▼
       Parse Host / Method / Path
                 │
                 ▼
       Match rules by priority
        ├─ Match → Return mock
        └─ No match → Default HTTP connection
                         └─ Not configured → X-Original-Host
                                               └─ Missing → 404
help.diagramJmsFlow:
Your app ──JMS──▶ Echo (Artemis) ──JMS──▶ ESB
                        │
                     Rule matched?
                     ├─ Yes → Reply mock to ReplyTo
                     └─ No  → Forward to ESB
help.diagramJmsReply:
Client ── 1. Send request (Queue: REQ) ──▶ Echo
Client ◀─ 2. Reply (Queue: ReplyTo) ───────── Echo
help.diagramPriority:
Rule sorting (higher value = higher priority)
1. priority field value
2. Exact path before wildcard (*)
3. targetHost specified before unspecified
4. Newer creation time first

Matching flow
1. Check rules in sorted order
2. Condition matches → return immediately
3. No condition → remember as fallback
4. Return fallback if nothing matches

help.title: Quick Start Guide
help.whatIsEchoDesc: Echo is a mock service that intercepts your HTTP/JMS requests and returns predefined mock responses, so you don't need real backend services during development.
help.step1: Click Add Rule in the top right
help.step4: Configure response content and status code
help.jmsTestDesc: Connect to tcp://localhost:61616 and send a message to the specified Queue
help.responseManagementDesc: Responses can be managed independently. Multiple rules can share the same response:
help.createNewResponseDesc: Edit response content directly in the rule
help.useExistingResponseDesc: Select an existing response for reuse
help.responsePageDesc: Manage all responses in one place
help.kbHint: Shortcuts are disabled when an input is focused (except Esc)
help.fieldTargetHost: Used only for rule matching (e.g., api.example.com). Leave empty to match all; it never changes the forwarding destination.
help.fieldPath: API path (e.g., /api/users). Use * to match all.
help.fieldDelay: Response delay in milliseconds to simulate network latency
help.fieldHeaders: Custom response headers in JSON format, e.g., {"Content-Type":"text/xml"}
help.condOperators: Operators: = equals, != not equals, *= contains, ~= regex
help.condMultiple: Use ; to combine multiple conditions (AND logic), e.g., type=VIP;level=gold
help.condOverviewDesc: Echo supports three types of conditions. Body conditions work for both HTTP and JMS. Query and Header conditions are HTTP only.
help.condAutoDetectDesc: Echo auto-detects the body format: starts with { → JSON, starts with < → XML. No manual configuration needed.
help.jmsFieldReplyQueue: Queue for sending replies. Leave empty to use the message's ReplyTo.
help.jmsCondMatch: Match message content (JSON/XML), same syntax as HTTP
help.jmsCondNote: JMS only supports Body conditions. Query and Header are not supported.
help.jmsReplyNote: Echo automatically reads the JMSReplyTo property and sends the response to the specified Queue
help.responseTemplateDesc: Response content supports Handlebars template syntax, auto-detected when {{ is present:
help.fakerHelpersDesc: Generate realistic fake data for mock responses. No external library needed.
help.wildcardNote: Wildcard rules (*) always act as fallback, unaffected by priority
help.tipWildcard: Wildcard Match: Use * for path or Queue as a default response
help.tipDelay: Delayed Response: Simulate network latency or slow services
help.tipBatchImport: Batch Import: Use Excel to quickly create multiple rules
help.tipTest: Rule Testing: Test your rule before saving to verify correct matching
help.tipTags: Tags: Use tags to organize rules by environment, team, or version
help.tipProtect: Rule Protection: Protected rules won't be auto-cleaned by the scheduled cleanup
help.tagsAndGroupsDesc: Add tags to rules for categorization. Switch to group view to browse rules by tag. Tags use key:value format.
help.ruleProtectionDesc: Protected rules are excluded from automatic cleanup. Use batch select to protect/unprotect multiple rules at once.
help.sseStreamingDesc: Rules can return Server-Sent Events streams. Enable SSE in the rule editor, then configure event sequences with individual delays and loop mode.
help.helperSplit: Split string into array, e.g., split ids by comma
help.faultInjectionDesc: Rules can simulate network faults. Set Fault Type in the rule editor to override normal response behavior.
help.faultConnectionReset: HTTP: Close connection without response. JMS: Skip reply message.
help.faultEmptyResponse: HTTP: Return configured status code with empty body. JMS: Send empty reply.
